_note: Content bank for Geometry Transformations. Rules are stated for the coordinate plane, about the origin unless a reflection line is named. Quiz answers were checked against the transform rules in assets/transform.js.

example.note: Every point moved right 3 and down 2. The triangle did not turn, flip, or change size.

lessons.orientation: Same — it still faces the same way
lessons.rule: (x, y) → (x + a, y + b). Add a to every x, add b to every y.
lessons.title: 1 · Translation — slide
lessons.watchOut: A negative b means DOWN, not up. Translating by (3, −2) moves right 3, down 2 — the sign on y is the vertical direction.
lessons.what: Slide every point of a figure the same distance in the same direction. No turning, no flipping, no resizing.

example.note: Only the y sign changed. The image is a mirror copy across the x-axis.

lessons.orientation: Reversed — a mirror image faces the other way
lessons.rule: Over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). Over the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y). Over y = x: (x, y) → (y, x). Over y = −x: (x, y) → (−y, −x).
lessons.title: 2 · Reflection — flip
lessons.watchOut: Do not mix up the axes: flipping over the x-axis changes the sign of y; flipping over the y-axis changes the sign of x. Flipping over y = x swaps x and y — it does not just change a sign.
lessons.what: Flip a figure over a line, like a mirror. Every point lands the same distance on the other side of the line.

lessons.orientation: Turned — but not mirrored (the order of the vertices around the figure stays the same)
lessons.rule: About the origin: 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). 180° (either way): (x, y) → (−x, −y). 270° clockwise is the same as 90° counterclockwise.
lessons.title: 3 · Rotation — turn
lessons.watchOut: Clockwise and counterclockwise are not interchangeable: 90° clockwise is (y, −x), 90° counterclockwise is (−y, x). If you swap them, every point lands in the wrong quadrant.
lessons.what: Turn a figure around a point (here, the origin) by an angle. The figure spins; it does not flip over.

lessons.congruent: Only if k = 1 — otherwise similar, not congruent

example.note: Every coordinate doubled, so every side doubled, but every angle stayed the same.

lessons.orientation: Same — it still faces the same way
lessons.rule: About the origin: (x, y) → (kx, ky). Multiply every coordinate by the scale factor k.
lessons.size: Changed — k > 1 enlarges, 0 < k < 1 reduces, k = 1 leaves it unchanged
lessons.title: 4 · Dilation — resize
lessons.watchOut: Dilation is the only one of the four that changes size. A figure and its dilation are similar (same shape, same angles), but they are congruent only when k = 1. Do not call a k = 2 image congruent.
lessons.what: Resize a figure from a center point (here, the origin) by a scale factor. The shape stays the same; the size does not.

quiz.question: Translate point (2, 3) by (−1, 4). What is the image?
Reflect point (4, −5) over the x-axis. What is the image?
Reflect point (−3, 2) over the y-axis. What is the image?
Reflect point (2, 5) over the line y = x. What is the image?
quiz.why: Over y = x, (x, y) → (y, x): (2, 5) → (5, 2). It swaps the coordinates; it does not just change a sign.

quiz.question: Rotate point (3, 4) by 90° clockwise about the origin. What is the image?
Rotate point (3, 4) by 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What is the image?
Rotate point (−2, 5) by 180° about the origin. What is the image?
Dilate point (2, −3) by a scale factor of 2 about the origin. What is the image?
Dilate point (6, 4) by a scale factor of 0.5 about the origin. What is the image?
quiz.why: (0.5·6, 0.5·4) = (3, 2). A factor below 1 shrinks the figure.

quiz.question: Dilate point (3, −2) by a scale factor of 3 about the origin. What is the image?
Point (2, 3) maps to (2, −3). Which transformation is this?
quiz.why: Only y changed sign, x stayed the same — that is a flip over the x-axis.

quiz.question: Point (−1, 4) maps to (1, 4). Which transformation is this?
quiz.why: Only x changed sign — a flip over the y-axis.

quiz.question: Point (2, 1) maps to (1, 2). Which transformation is this?
quiz.why: The coordinates swapped — that is a flip over y = x, not a sign change.

quiz.question: Point (3, 2) maps to (−2, 3). Which rotation is this?
quiz.why: 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x) = (−2, 3). The clockwise version would give (2, −3).

quiz.question: Point (1, 2) maps to (2, 4). Which transformation is this?
quiz.why: Every coordinate doubled — (kx, ky) with k = 2.

choices: It is congruent to the original
It is similar to the original, but not congruent (unless k = 1)
Its side lengths stay the same
quiz.question: A figure is dilated by k = 2. Which statement is true?
quiz.why: Dilation keeps the shape and the angles but scales every side by k, so the image is similar, not congruent.
